pot-odds.definition: The ratio of the call amount to the pot after calling, i.e. the minimum equity a call needs to break even.

implied-odds.definition: Pot odds extended by the future chips you expect to win after hitting your draw.

reverse-implied-odds.definition: The risk of hitting your draw and still losing a bigger pot, as with non-nut flushes or weak-kicker top pair.

equity.definition: Your share of the pot based on win probability across all possible runouts.

expected-value.definition: The probability-weighted average result of a decision, the common unit for comparing every action.

outs.definition: Unknown cards remaining in the deck that make your hand beat your opponent's range.

set-mining.definition: Calling cheaply with a small pocket pair, hoping to flop a set and win a deep stack.

combinatorics.definition: Counting ranges with C(n,k): 6 combos per pair, 4 per suited hand and 12 per offsuit hand.

blocker.definition: Holding a card that removes combinations from your opponent's range, changing its value and bluff density.

range.definition: The full distribution of hands an opponent can hold given the actions taken so far.

range-advantage.definition: One side's overall range has higher average equity, usually converted into a higher betting frequency.

nut-advantage.definition: One side holds more of the strongest combinations, usually converted into a larger sizing ceiling.

polarization.definition: A betting range made of strong value and pure bluffs with little middle strength, which prefers large sizes.

linear-range.definition: A contiguous strength slice that includes many medium hands, which prefers small and medium sizes.

continuation-bet.definition: A flop bet by the preflop raiser that continues the initiative.

check-raise.definition: Checking, then raising after an opponent bets, used to polarize and to protect the checking range.

probe-bet.definition: A bet by the previous street's caller after the aggressor checks, testing the strength of that range.

overbet.definition: A bet larger than the pot, sustainable only when you own the nut advantage and its bluff capacity.

blocking-bet.definition: A small out-of-position bet that caps the opponent's raise and bet sizes, at the cost of revealing strength.

minimum-defense-frequency.definition: The minimum continue frequency that makes any two cards indifferent to bluffing, equal to pot divided by pot plus bet.

alpha.definition: The fold frequency a bluff needs to break even, bet divided by pot plus bet, the complement of MDF.

nash-equilibrium.definition: A strategy profile where no player gains by deviating alone, the mathematical basis of GTO play.

gto.definition: Game-theory optimal, an unexploitable baseline used to measure deviations rather than a script to copy.

mixed-strategy.definition: Splitting one hand across several actions by frequency so opponents cannot infer your holding.

indifference.definition: In equilibrium a hand's actions have equal EV, so it can mix freely without being exploited.

node-locking.definition: Fixing an opponent's biased behavior at one node in a solver to compute the maximum exploit.

exploitative-play.definition: Targeted adjustments against systematic deviations, trading some unexploitability for higher EV.

icm.definition: The Independent Chip Model, converting stacks into finish probabilities and prize EV to capture diminishing chip value.

chip-ev.definition: Expected value measured in chips, identical to money EV in cash games.

dollar-ev.definition: Expected value converted through the prize structure, the correct measure for tournament decisions.

spr.definition: Effective stack divided by the current pot, setting how many streets and commitment thresholds are available.

geometric-sizing.definition: Growing each street's bet by a fixed ratio so the stack is exactly committed across the planned streets.

equity-realization.definition: The share of all-in equity actually collected, governed by position, SPR and board texture.

vpip.definition: Voluntarily put money in pot, the share of hands played, measuring range width.

pfr.definition: Preflop raise percentage; the gap to VPIP reveals a passive calling tendency.

aggression-factor.definition: Postflop bets and raises divided by calls, measuring how active a player is.

wtsd.definition: Went to showdown percentage, measuring fold tendency and showdown range width.

three-bet.definition: A re-raise over an open, used to contest the pot and the initiative with a polarized or linear range.

four-bet.definition: A re-raise over a 3-bet that trends polarized and stack-committing at low SPR.

squeeze.definition: A 3-bet after an open and at least one caller, applying pressure to both players.

cold-call.definition: Calling a raise without any blind invested, usually requiring a stronger hand than defending a blind.

gap-concept.definition: Facing demonstrated strength, the hand standard for continuing must exceed the standard for opening.

position.definition: The information and equity-realization edge from acting later postflop, strongest on the button.

tilt.definition: Systematic decision drift caused by emotion or fatigue, the most expensive leak for amateurs.

bankroll-management.definition: Using buy-in counts and move-up rules to keep risk of ruin and psychological pressure tolerable.

risk-of-ruin.definition: The probability of losing the bankroll given win rate, standard deviation and size, approximated by exp(-2 mu B / sigma^2).

kelly-criterion.definition: The stake fraction f* = (bp - q)/b that maximizes long-run growth; practical play uses half Kelly.

variance.definition: The spread of results around expectation; it dominates the short run while expectation dominates the long run.

downswing.definition: A sustained losing stretch even winning players face, a mathematical certainty of variance rather than a skill loss.

rake.definition: The house fee taken as a share of the pot, directly lowering net win rate and raising sample and bankroll needs.

ante.definition: Forced dead money posted every hand, raising the pot P so steals get cheaper and defense obligations heavier.

straddle.definition: A voluntary extra forced bet beyond the blinds that also changes action order and position.

multiway-pot.definition: A pot with three or more players where bluff success falls exponentially and nut potential comes first.

heads-up.definition: A pot or game with only two players left, where position and blind structure differ completely from multiway play.

bubble.definition: The tournament stage just before the money, where ICM pressure peaks.

fold-equity.definition: The expected value gained when opponents fold, the profit source of bluffs and semi-bluffs.

thin-value.definition: A value bet whose called range is only slightly weaker than your hand, requiring precise range judgment.
